options.a: Pass the state exam and practice while the license is being issued
options.b: Hold an active license and open a separate office under their own name
options.c: Be associated with a licensed broker and hold an active license
options.d: Complete the 77-hour course and join a local MLS as a member

distractorExplanations.a: Passing the exam is not licensure; New York salespersons may act only after the license is issued and associated with a broker.
distractorExplanations.b: A salesperson cannot run their own office or brokerage; New York requires association with and supervision by a licensed broker.
distractorExplanations.d: MLS membership is not a licensing step; after the 77-hour course and exam the salesperson still needs a license and a sponsoring broker.

options.a: Deposits several buyers' earnest money into one escrow account
options.b: Deposits earnest money into an interest-bearing escrow account
options.c: Keeps escrow records at a branch office instead of the main office
options.d: Mixes client trust/escrow funds with personal or operating funds

distractorExplanations.a: A single escrow account holding several clients' deposits is permitted; commingling is mixing client money with the broker's own funds.
distractorExplanations.b: Interest-bearing escrow accounts are allowed with proper disclosure; commingling means mixing escrow funds with personal or business funds.
distractorExplanations.c: Where records are stored is a recordkeeping question; commingling is about mixing client funds with the broker's own money.

options.a: Licensees should carry their pocket card and produce it upon request
options.b: Pocket cards are issued by the broker and replace the wall license
options.c: Pocket cards are required only for brokers, not for salespersons
options.d: Pocket cards must be displayed in every advertisement the agent runs

distractorExplanations.b: NY pocket cards are issued by the Department of State, and the license itself is still kept at the broker's office; the card does not replace it.
distractorExplanations.c: Both brokers and salespersons are issued pocket cards in New York and must carry them when acting as licensees.
distractorExplanations.d: Ads must identify the brokerage, but no rule requires the pocket card itself to appear in advertisements.

options.a: May keep working under the suspended broker until their own renewal date
options.b: Cannot continue licensed activity under that broker until re-associated
options.c: May keep working if the office manager holds an associate broker license
options.d: Lose their own licenses and must retake the licensing exam

distractorExplanations.a: A salesperson's authority depends on an active sponsoring broker; it does not continue until the salesperson's renewal date.
distractorExplanations.c: An associate broker cannot step in as sponsor while the principal broker is suspended; salespersons must associate with an active broker.
distractorExplanations.d: The salesperson's license is not revoked; it cannot be used until they associate with a new broker, and no re-exam is required.

options.a: Host open houses alone and answer buyers' price questions
options.b: Show properties if a licensee is reachable by phone
options.c: Perform clerical tasks that do not require a license
options.d: Receive a share of commissions for helping close the deal

distractorExplanations.a: Hosting an open house and discussing price is licensed activity; an unlicensed assistant may not do it.
distractorExplanations.b: Showing property requires a license; having a licensee available by phone does not authorize an unlicensed assistant to show.
distractorExplanations.d: Commission splits go to licensees; paying an unlicensed assistant a share of commission for brokerage work is prohibited.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-license-l.explanation: Unlicensed staff may do support work but may not perform activities that require a real estate license. Examples include scheduling appointments and filing.

options.a: Prohibited; ads must properly identify the brokerage
options.b: Allowed if the salesperson's name and phone number appear
options.c: Allowed for rentals but prohibited for sales listings
options.d: Allowed on social media if a link leads to the brokerage

distractorExplanations.b: NY ads must identify the brokerage; listing only the salesperson's contact details still makes it a blind ad.
distractorExplanations.c: The blind ad prohibition applies to rentals and sales alike; a rental ad must still identify the brokerage.
distractorExplanations.d: Social media posts must themselves identify the brokerage; a link elsewhere does not cure a blind ad.

options.a: A written fee agreement, even if the recipient is unlicensed
options.b: Compliance with RESPA and New York rules, including disclosure
options.c: Payment from the title company to the broker for each referral
options.d: Disclosure on the Closing Disclosure, which makes any referral fee lawful

distractorExplanations.a: A written agreement does not legalize paying an unlicensed person for brokerage referrals; New York requires the recipient be licensed.
distractorExplanations.c: A title company paying a broker per referral is exactly the kickback RESPA Section 8 prohibits, not a lawful referral fee.
distractorExplanations.d: Disclosure does not cure a RESPA kickback; payments for referrals of settlement services are prohibited even if disclosed.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-license-l.explanation: Fee-sharing for real estate and settlement services is tightly regulated; secret unlicensed payments are illegal. New York also limits referral fees to properly licensed recipients.

options.a: Fair housing protections enforced by the Division of Human Rights
options.b: Property condition disclosure duties for residential sellers
options.c: Licensing and regulation of real estate brokers and salespersons
options.d: Recording of deeds and mortgages with the county clerk

distractorExplanations.a: Fair housing in NY is in the Executive Law (Human Rights Law), not Article 12-A, which covers broker and salesperson licensing.
distractorExplanations.b: The Property Condition Disclosure Act is Article 14 of the Real Property Law, not Article 12-A's licensing framework.
distractorExplanations.d: Recording is governed by Real Property Law Article 9, not Article 12-A, which regulates licensing of brokers and salespersons.

options.a: Legal if the seller signs a written net agreement
options.b: Legal for commercial property but not residential
options.c: Allowed if the broker's excess is capped at 6%
options.d: Illegal / prohibited as a listing method

distractorExplanations.a: New York prohibits net listings outright; a signed written agreement does not make the arrangement lawful.
distractorExplanations.b: The net listing ban is not limited to residential property; it applies to New York listings generally.
distractorExplanations.c: No cap cures a net listing; the excess-over-net structure itself is prohibited in New York.

options.a: At the first substantive contact with a buyer or seller
options.b: Before the buyer signs the purchase contract or binder
options.c: Only after the client signs an exclusive agency agreement
options.d: At closing, together with the commission statement

distractorExplanations.b: Waiting until the binder or contract is too late; New York requires the agency disclosure form at the first substantive contact.
distractorExplanations.c: The disclosure comes before any agreement is signed; it is given at the first substantive contact, not after an exclusive contract.
distractorExplanations.d: Agency disclosure at closing defeats its purpose; it must be given at the first substantive contact with the consumer.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-license-l.explanation: NY agency disclosure timing rules require early, proper disclosure of the licensee's role. The contact concerns a specific property, and the form is required at that point.

options.a: Listing a P.O. box as the office address on the license
options.b: Maintaining a compliant office that meets DOS requirements
options.c: Letting each salesperson register a home office instead
options.d: Registering an office only if the broker employs salespersons

distractorExplanations.a: A P.O. box is not a place of business; New York brokers must maintain a physical office with the license and sign displayed.
distractorExplanations.c: Salespersons' home offices are not the broker's place of business; the broker must maintain the principal office of record.
distractorExplanations.d: Every NY broker must maintain a place of business, whether or not salespersons are associated with the firm.

options.a: An offer that becomes binding once a buyer agrees to the price
options.b: An employment contract between the seller and the broker
options.c: A purchase contract between the seller and the buyer
options.d: An agency agreement between the buyer and the broker

distractorExplanations.a: A listing hires the broker; it is not an offer to buyers and does not bind the seller to a sale when a buyer agrees.
distractorExplanations.c: The sale contract is between seller and buyer; the listing is a separate agreement between the seller and the broker.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes buyer agency; a listing agreement is the seller's employment contract with the listing broker.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Listings hire the brokerage to market the property; they do not convey title or create a loan. It authorizes the broker to market the property and find a buyer.

options.a: The listing broker earns a commission if the property sells during the term
options.b: The broker earns a commission unless the seller finds the buyer
options.c: Any broker who procures the buyer earns the commission from the seller
options.d: The broker is paid when the buyer's agent signs a cooperation agreement

distractorExplanations.b: That is an exclusive agency listing; under exclusive right-to-sell the broker is paid even if the seller finds the buyer.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes an open listing, where the procuring broker is paid; exclusive right-to-sell names one listing broker.
distractorExplanations.d: Cooperation between brokers affects splits, not entitlement; the listing broker's right turns on a sale during the term.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Exclusive right-to-sell is the most protective listing form for the broker's commission entitlement. This holds regardless of who finds the buyer, per the contract.

options.a: Notarized and recorded before they become binding
options.b: In writing and signed by the party to be charged
options.c: In writing and signed by both brokers involved
options.d: Witnessed by two people if made orally

distractorExplanations.a: Notarization and recording are not required for enforceability; the Statute of Frauds requires a signed writing.
distractorExplanations.c: Brokers are not parties to the sale contract; the signature that matters is that of the party to be charged.
distractorExplanations.d: Witnesses do not save an oral real estate sale contract; the Statute of Frauds requires a signed writing.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Conveyances and sale contracts for real property generally must be written to be enforceable. Limited exceptions, such as part performance, exist.

options.a: Race, color, religion, sex, national origin, and personal credit history
options.b: Race, religion, national origin, and political party affiliation
options.c: Race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, and disability
options.d: Familial status and disability, but not religion or sex

distractorExplanations.a: Credit history is not a protected class; lenders and landlords may consider it, unlike the federal protected classes.
distractorExplanations.b: Political affiliation is not a fair housing protected class; the federal list is race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability.
distractorExplanations.d: Religion and sex are federally protected classes; omitting them misstates the Fair Housing Act.

options.a: Inducing owners to sell by warning that a protected class is moving into the area
options.b: Refusing to show a listing to a buyer who lacks a preapproval letter
options.c: Charging different loan terms to borrowers in minority neighborhoods
options.d: Guiding prospects toward or away from neighborhoods based on protected class

distractorExplanations.a: That is blockbusting; steering is channeling buyers toward or away from areas based on protected characteristics.
distractorExplanations.b: Requiring proof of financing applied evenly is a business practice, not steering, which turns on protected-class traits.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes redlining or discriminatory lending; steering is a licensee directing housing choices by protected class.

options.a: A preliminary agreement that may lead to a full contract
options.b: A binding contract that replaces any attorney-drafted agreement
options.c: A deposit receipt that transfers equitable title at signing
options.d: A listing addendum signed by the seller and listing broker

distractorExplanations.b: In NY practice a binder is usually preliminary and nonbinding; attorneys then prepare the full contract of sale.
distractorExplanations.c: A binder does not transfer equitable title; equitable title passes under the executed contract of sale, not the binder.
distractorExplanations.d: A binder is an offer document between buyer and seller, not an addendum to the seller's listing agreement.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: NY commonly uses binders/offers followed by attorney-prepared contracts; the binder is not the deed. Attorneys then prepare the full contract of sale.

options.a: It becomes the broker's commission once the binder is signed
options.b: It shows good faith and is typically held in escrow
options.c: It must be paid directly to the seller at contract signing
options.d: It is legally required and must equal 10% of the price

distractorExplanations.a: Earnest money is the buyer's deposit held in trust; the broker cannot take it as commission when the binder is signed.
distractorExplanations.c: Paying the seller directly defeats escrow; the deposit is held by an escrow agent until closing or authorized release.
distractorExplanations.d: No law sets a mandatory earnest money amount; 10% is a common NY contract deposit by custom, not a legal requirement.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Earnest money is security for performance, not an automatic broker fee or substitute for the purchase price. Funds stay in escrow pending contract performance or authorized release.

options.a: Directing buyers toward or away from neighborhoods based on their race or religion
options.b: Refusing to make loans in areas with large minority populations
options.c: Inducing panic selling by suggesting protected-class entry will lower values
options.d: Advertising a home with words that state a racial preference

distractorExplanations.a: That is steering; blockbusting is inducing owners to sell by claiming protected-class entry will hurt values.
distractorExplanations.b: That is redlining by lenders; blockbusting is panic peddling to owners about protected classes moving in.
distractorExplanations.d: Discriminatory advertising violates fair housing, but blockbusting specifically means panic peddling to induce sales.

options.a: Full fiduciary duties identical to those owed to the client
options.b: Confidentiality about price but no duty to disclose defects
options.c: Honesty, but no duty to disclose known material defects
options.d: Honesty, fairness, and disclosure of known material facts

distractorExplanations.a: Customers do not receive fiduciary loyalty or confidentiality; those duties run to the client the licensee represents.
distractorExplanations.b: Customers are owed disclosure of known material defects; confidentiality and advocacy are owed to the client.
distractorExplanations.c: Even a customer must be told of known material facts; honesty without disclosure of known defects falls short.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Customers get fair dealing; clients get fiduciary duties. Licensees must still be honest with customers. Customers do not receive full fiduciary loyalty.

options.a: The right, but not the obligation, to purchase on stated terms
options.b: The obligation to buy if the optionor finds no better offer
options.c: A right of first refusal to match any third-party offer
options.d: Equitable title to the property from the day the option is signed

distractorExplanations.b: An optionee is not obligated to buy; the optionor is the party bound to sell if the option is exercised.
distractorExplanations.c: A right of first refusal lets the holder match an offer; an option gives a right to buy on stated terms.
distractorExplanations.d: Equitable title passes under a sale contract, not an unexercised option; the optionee holds a contractual right.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Options create a unilateral right to buy; exercise is optional for the optionee. The right must be exercised within the option period.

options.a: Describing the home as a 'great starter home' with a large fenced yard
options.b: Using phrases that express preference for or against a protected class
options.c: Noting that the building has a wheelchair-accessible entrance
options.d: Stating that the apartment is a 'no smoking' unit

distractorExplanations.a: Describing the property's features or appeal is lawful; the violation is stating a preference about who may live there.
distractorExplanations.c: Describing accessibility features is lawful and encouraged; it does not express a preference against a protected class.
distractorExplanations.d: Smoking is not a protected class, so a no-smoking policy is a lawful rule, not a discriminatory preference.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-contracts.explanation: Ads may describe the property, not discriminatory preferences about who may buy/rent. Examples: 'no children' or 'Christians only'.

options.a: Share it, since motivation is a material fact buyers are owed
options.b: Share it if the buyer's offer is already at the asking price
options.c: Avoid disclosing confidential client information unless authorized
options.d: Answer truthfully, since customers are owed full disclosure

distractorExplanations.a: Seller motivation is confidential, not a material property defect; the seller's agent may not reveal it without consent.
distractorExplanations.b: A full-price offer does not release confidentiality; the seller's motivation still needs the seller's authorization.
distractorExplanations.d: Customers are owed honesty about material facts, not the client's confidences such as motivation or bottom price.

options.a: A government-insured loan that meets FHA underwriting guidelines
options.b: A non-government-insured loan that meets GSE guidelines
options.c: Any loan that exceeds the Fannie Mae loan limit for the county
options.d: A non-government loan that fails GSE rules and stays in portfolio

distractorExplanations.a: FHA loans are government-insured; conventional loans are not, and conforming means meeting Fannie/Freddie standards.
distractorExplanations.c: A loan above the conforming limit is a jumbo, nonconforming loan; conforming loans fall within GSE limits.
distractorExplanations.d: Portfolio loans that miss GSE guidelines are nonconforming; conforming means eligible for sale to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-v.explanation: Conventional loans are not FHA/VA insured/guaranteed; conforming means they meet agency size/guidelines. GSE here means Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac.

options.a: Principal, Interest, Title, and Inspection
options.b: Points, Interest, Taxes, and Insurance
options.c: Principal, Interest, Taxes, and Insurance
options.d: Principal, Index, Term, and Interest

distractorExplanations.a: Title and inspection are closing costs, not monthly payment items; PITI's T and I are property taxes and insurance.
distractorExplanations.b: Points are paid once at closing; the first P in PITI is principal, which is repaid in each monthly payment.
distractorExplanations.d: Index and term describe adjustable-rate loan features; PITI lists the four parts of the monthly housing payment.

options.a: Cost approach (depreciated cost)
options.b: Income capitalization approach
options.c: Highest and best use analysis
options.d: Sales comparison (market) approach

distractorExplanations.a: The cost approach estimates land value plus depreciated replacement cost; it does not rely on recent comparable sales.
distractorExplanations.b: The income approach capitalizes net operating income; it suits rental property and is not built on recent sales of similar homes.
distractorExplanations.c: Highest and best use is a premise analyzed before valuation, not an approach that adjusts recent comparable sales.

options.a: Are prepaid interest that can reduce the note rate
options.b: Are a tax-deductible fee equal to 1% of the purchase price
options.c: Are paid by the lender to the broker for each referral
options.d: Are an annual charge added to the escrow for taxes

distractorExplanations.b: One point equals 1% of the loan amount, not the purchase price; deductibility is a separate tax question.
distractorExplanations.c: Lender payments to brokers for referrals are RESPA kickbacks; points are charges the borrower or seller pays the lender.
distractorExplanations.d: Points are a one-time charge at closing, not a recurring escrow item like taxes and insurance.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-v.explanation: One point = 1% of the loan; discount points buy down rate; origination points are lender fees. Origination points instead cover lender fees.

options.a: An FHA loan is made with the minimum 3.5% down payment
options.b: A conventional loan has a high LTV (often above 80%)
options.c: A VA loan is made with no down payment
options.d: A conventional loan has an LTV of 80% or lower

distractorExplanations.a: FHA loans carry the FHA mortgage insurance premium (MIP), not private mortgage insurance from a private insurer.
distractorExplanations.c: VA loans have no monthly mortgage insurance; the VA guarantee and a funding fee take its place.
distractorExplanations.d: At 80% LTV or below PMI is generally not required; it applies when the conventional loan exceeds 80% LTV.

options.a: Interest-only payments followed by a single principal payment
options.b: Payments that rise each year as the interest rate adjusts
options.c: Periodic payments that pay down principal over the loan term
options.d: Spreading the cost of a building's wear over its useful life

distractorExplanations.a: That is a straight (term) loan; amortization reduces principal with every scheduled payment over the term.
distractorExplanations.b: Rate adjustment describes an ARM; amortization is the gradual repayment of principal through scheduled payments.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes depreciation for valuation or tax purposes; loan amortization is paying down principal over the term.

options.a: A USPAP appraisal that a lender may rely on for the loan
options.b: A broker price opinion that must follow appraisal standards
options.c: An assessment of value used to set the annual property tax
options.d: A marketing/pricing opinion using comps—not a formal appraisal

distractorExplanations.a: A CMA is not a USPAP appraisal; lenders require an appraisal by a licensed or certified appraiser.
distractorExplanations.b: A CMA is a pricing tool, and neither a CMA nor a BPO is held to USPAP appraisal standards.
distractorExplanations.c: Tax assessments are made by the municipal assessor; a CMA is a licensee's pricing opinion from comparable sales.

options.a: Delivered by the seller (grantor) to the buyer (grantee)
options.b: Delivered by the buyer (grantee) to the seller (grantor)
options.c: Signed by the buyer and recorded before delivery
options.d: Issued by the county clerk after the mortgage is recorded

distractorExplanations.b: That reverses the parties; the grantor is the seller who conveys title, and the grantee is the buyer who receives it.
distractorExplanations.c: The grantor signs the deed, and title passes on delivery and acceptance; recording follows to give notice.
distractorExplanations.d: The county clerk records deeds but does not issue them; the seller executes and delivers the deed at closing.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-v.explanation: Title transfers by delivery of a properly executed deed meeting statutory formalities. Delivery and acceptance transfer title.

options.a: Divide the broker's commission between buyer and seller
options.b: Allocate items like taxes and rents fairly between buyer and seller
options.c: Calculate the lender's points as a share of the buyer's purchase price
options.d: Allocate the transfer tax between buyer and seller by custom

distractorExplanations.a: Commission is paid under the listing agreement; prorations split ongoing charges like taxes and rents by ownership period.
distractorExplanations.c: Points are a percentage of the loan amount charged by the lender; prorations allocate recurring items as of the closing date.
distractorExplanations.d: NY transfer tax is generally a seller cost by statute, not a prorated item; prorations cover taxes, rents, and similar ongoing charges.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-v.explanation: Prorations split ongoing charges/credits so each party pays their ownership period share. The split is computed as of the closing date.

options.a: A government guarantee that requires no down payment for eligible veterans
options.b: Funding from the federal government directly to the borrower
options.c: Mortgage insurance through FHA and more flexible qualifying guidelines
options.d: Private mortgage insurance that cancels at 80% loan-to-value

distractorExplanations.a: No-down-payment loans for veterans are VA loans; FHA loans need at least 3.5% down and carry FHA mortgage insurance.
distractorExplanations.b: FHA does not lend money; it insures loans made by approved private lenders.
distractorExplanations.d: Cancellation at 80% LTV describes conventional PMI; FHA uses its own mortgage insurance premium under different rules.

options.a: A busy highway built next door to the home
options.b: Peeling paint and worn carpet in the bedrooms
options.c: A roof that has reached the end of its life
options.d: An outdated floor plan or inadequate closets

distractorExplanations.a: Loss from a nearby highway is external (economic) obsolescence, arising outside the property, not functional obsolescence.
distractorExplanations.b: That is curable physical deterioration from wear, not a design flaw within the property.
distractorExplanations.c: An aging roof is physical deterioration; functional obsolescence is loss from outdated or poor design.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-v.explanation: Functional obsolescence is loss from outdated/poor design within the property. Such design flaws hurt marketability.

options.a: A large final payment that pays off remaining principal
options.b: A large first payment made at closing to lower the rate
options.c: A payment that grows each year under a graduated plan
options.d: An extra principal payment that shortens a fully amortized loan

distractorExplanations.b: Paying up front to lower the rate describes discount points; a balloon is the large final payment at maturity.
distractorExplanations.c: Graduated payments rise gradually over time; a balloon is a single lump sum that retires the remaining balance at the end.
distractorExplanations.d: Voluntary prepayment on a fully amortizing loan is not a balloon; a balloon arises when the loan leaves a balance due at maturity.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-v.explanation: Partially amortizing loans leave a balance due at maturity—the balloon. It arises when the loan does not fully amortize.

options.a: Losses from boundary disputes that a current survey would reveal
options.b: Covered defects in title that were not discovered in the title search
options.c: Defects in the home's structure that the inspector missed
options.d: Liens the buyer agreed to assume in the contract of sale

distractorExplanations.a: Standard title policies except matters an accurate survey would show; survey issues need a survey endorsement or separate coverage.
distractorExplanations.c: Physical defects are an inspection or warranty issue; title insurance covers title risks like forged deeds and unknown liens.
distractorExplanations.d: Liens the buyer knowingly assumed are listed exceptions; title insurance covers undiscovered covered defects.

options.a: The Loan Estimate issued within three business days of application
options.b: The lender's commitment letter for the mortgage
options.c: The Closing Disclosure (TRID) / settlement statement
options.d: The title commitment issued by the title insurer

distractorExplanations.a: The Loan Estimate is an early cost estimate given within three business days of application; the CD shows final figures.
distractorExplanations.b: A commitment letter states loan approval terms; it does not itemize final cash due and credits for each party.
distractorExplanations.d: A title commitment lists title conditions and exceptions, not the buyer's and seller's final funds and credits.

options.a: Personal property that has become real property
options.b: Personal property that the seller may remove before closing
options.c: A trade fixture that belongs to the landlord at lease end
options.d: Any item listed separately on the bill of sale

distractorExplanations.b: That describes chattels; a fixture has become real property and transfers with the land unless excluded.
distractorExplanations.c: Trade fixtures belong to the tenant and may be removed before the lease ends; they are an exception to the fixture rule.
distractorExplanations.d: Items on a bill of sale are personal property transferred separately; a fixture passes with the deed as real property.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Fixtures (e.g., built-in appliances, chandelier wired in) transfer with the realty unless excluded. Courts weigh annexation, intent, and adaptation.

options.a: Ownership that ends if a stated condition is violated
options.b: The most complete bundle of rights lasting potentially forever
options.c: Ownership for the life of the owner, then passing to a remainderman
options.d: Ownership of a unit plus an interest in common areas

distractorExplanations.a: That is a fee simple defeasible; fee simple absolute carries no conditions that can end the estate.
distractorExplanations.c: That is a life estate; fee simple absolute is inheritable and not limited to one person's lifetime.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes condominium ownership, a form of holding rather than the definition of the fee simple absolute estate.

options.a: Benefits a named person and ends when that person dies
options.b: Benefits the servient tenement and ends at its sale
options.c: Benefits a dominant tenement and runs with the land
options.d: Is a revocable permission to cross the land

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a personal easement in gross; an appurtenant easement benefits land and passes with the dominant estate.
distractorExplanations.b: The servient tenement is burdened, not benefited, and the easement does not end when the servient land is sold.
distractorExplanations.d: Revocable permission is a license, not an easement; an appurtenant easement is an interest that runs with the land.

options.a: Building construction standards such as wiring and plumbing
options.b: Private restrictions that a developer records in the deeds
options.c: The assessed value used to calculate property taxes
options.d: Land use, density, and building bulk/height within districts

distractorExplanations.a: Construction standards are set by building codes; zoning controls land use, density, and bulk within districts.
distractorExplanations.b: Recorded deed restrictions are private controls; zoning is public land-use regulation under the police power.
distractorExplanations.c: Assessment is a tax function of the assessor; zoning regulates how land in each district may be used.

options.a: Authorization to deviate from a zoning requirement
options.b: A change in the zoning classification of a single parcel
options.c: Permission to continue a use that predates the current zoning
options.d: Approval for a use the zoning code allows by special permit

distractorExplanations.b: Changing a parcel's zoning district is a rezoning (spot zoning if singled out), not relief from one requirement.
distractorExplanations.c: That is a nonconforming use (grandfathered); a variance grants relief from a requirement due to hardship.
distractorExplanations.d: That is a special use (conditional use) permit; a variance deviates from the code because of hardship.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Variances grant relief from strict zoning application in specific hardship cases. It is granted for unnecessary hardship (standards vary).

options.a: Lot and block numbers from a recorded subdivision plat
options.b: Distances and directions from a point of beginning
options.c: Townships and sections from government survey lines
options.d: Street address and tax map number from the assessor

distractorExplanations.a: That is the lot-and-block (recorded plat) method, not metes and bounds.
distractorExplanations.c: That is the rectangular (government) survey system, which New York does not use as its primary method.
distractorExplanations.d: A street address or tax map number identifies a parcel informally; metes and bounds trace its boundaries by courses and distances.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Metes and bounds are survey-based boundary descriptions common for irregular parcels. The description runs around the parcel back to that point.

options.a: Undivided shares that pass to each owner's heirs at death
options.b: Ownership available only to married spouses
options.c: Right of survivorship among joint tenants
options.d: Unequal shares based on each owner's contribution

distractorExplanations.a: Passing shares to heirs describes tenancy in common; joint tenants' interests pass to surviving co-owners.
distractorExplanations.b: Ownership limited to spouses describes tenancy by the entirety; joint tenancy can be held by any co-owners.
distractorExplanations.d: Joint tenancy requires equal interests (unity of interest); unequal shares point to tenancy in common.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Joint tenancy's hallmark is survivorship; tenancy in common lacks survivorship. The four unities are typically required.

options.a: A right to use another's land for a specific purpose
options.b: A recorded restriction on how the owner may use the land
options.c: A structure that extends onto a neighbor's property
options.d: A financial claim against property as security for a debt

distractorExplanations.a: A right to use another's land is an easement; a lien is a monetary claim securing a debt.
distractorExplanations.b: Use restrictions are deed restrictions or covenants, which are nonmonetary encumbrances, not liens.
distractorExplanations.c: A structure crossing the boundary is an encroachment, a physical encumbrance, not a financial claim.

options.a: Proper recording in the public land records
options.b: Delivery of the deed to the grantee at closing
options.c: Notarizing the deed in front of both parties
options.d: Filing a copy with the local tax assessor's office

distractorExplanations.b: Delivery passes title between the parties, but notice to the world comes from recording in the public records.
distractorExplanations.c: Acknowledgment lets a deed be recorded, but it is recording itself that gives constructive notice.
distractorExplanations.d: The assessor's records are for taxation; constructive notice comes from recording with the county clerk.

options.a: A right to cross a neighbor's land to reach a road
options.b: A structure or improvement that extends onto another's land
options.c: A recorded claim against the land for unpaid work
options.d: Gaining title by open, hostile use of a neighbor's land

distractorExplanations.a: A right of access over another's land is an easement, a lawful interest, not an unauthorized intrusion.
distractorExplanations.c: A claim for unpaid work is a mechanic's lien, a monetary encumbrance, not a physical intrusion.
distractorExplanations.d: Gaining title through hostile use is adverse possession; an encroachment is the improvement crossing the line.

options.a: Shares in a corporation plus a proprietary lease for the unit
options.b: The unit in fee, with common areas owned by the developer
options.c: The unit in fee plus an undivided interest in common elements
options.d: A leasehold in the unit plus a share of the common charges

distractorExplanations.a: Shares and a proprietary lease describe co-op ownership; condominium owners hold a deeded unit.
distractorExplanations.b: Condo common elements are owned by the unit owners as undivided interests, not retained by the developer.
distractorExplanations.d: Condo owners hold the unit in fee, not a leasehold; common charges are a cost, not an ownership interest.

options.a: A deed to the unit plus an undivided interest in common elements
options.b: A deed to the building held jointly with the other residents
options.c: A long-term ground lease from the building's owner
options.d: Shares in the cooperative corporation and a proprietary lease

distractorExplanations.a: A deed plus common-element interest describes condo ownership; co-op buyers receive shares and a proprietary lease.
distractorExplanations.b: The co-op corporation holds the deed to the building; residents own shares, not a joint deeded interest.
distractorExplanations.c: A ground lease conveys land use rights, often to a developer; co-op residents hold shares and a proprietary lease.

options.a: The government's power to take private property for public use
options.b: The government's power to tax real property to fund services
options.c: The government's power to regulate land use through zoning
options.d: The state's right to take property when an owner dies without heirs

distractorExplanations.b: That is the power of taxation; eminent domain is the power to take private property for public use.
distractorExplanations.c: Regulation through zoning is the police power; eminent domain takes title or interests and requires just compensation.
distractorExplanations.d: Property reverting to the state when there are no heirs is escheat, not eminent domain.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Takings require public use/purpose and just compensation under constitutional standards. Just compensation must be paid.

options.a: That the property's title is free of recorded liens
options.b: That a building/unit meets applicable codes for occupancy
options.c: That the building passed the buyer's home inspection
options.d: That the zoning board has granted a use variance

distractorExplanations.a: Clear title is shown by a title search and policy, not by a certificate of occupancy.
distractorExplanations.c: A home inspection is a private report for the buyer; a CO is issued by the municipal building authority.
distractorExplanations.d: A variance is zoning relief from a board; a CO certifies code compliance for lawful occupancy.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: COs are municipal/code compliance documents allowing lawful occupancy. The CO is issued by the local building authority.

options.a: Radon gas (homes built before 1950)
options.b: Chinese drywall (homes built after 2010)
options.c: Lead-based paint (pre-1978 housing)
options.d: Polybutylene pipes (homes built after 2000)

distractorExplanations.a: Radon depends on soil and geology, not home age; the pre-1978 federal disclosure rule applies to lead-based paint.
distractorExplanations.b: Defective imported drywall dates to about 2001-2009 construction, and no federal disclosure rule like the lead rule applies.
distractorExplanations.d: Polybutylene piping was installed roughly 1978 to 1995 and is not covered by a federal disclosure rule like pre-1978 lead paint.

ny-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Federal lead disclosure applies to most pre-1978 residential target housing; other hazards (asbestos, mold) also matter. Related federal disclosure rules apply to sales and leases.
